blind_cases.prompt: A trolley is initially at x=+5 m with v=−4 m/s. Its measured acceleration–time graph has horizontal segments: +3 m/s² for 0≤t<2 s, 0 for 2≤t<5 s, −2 m/s² for 5≤t≤8 s. Use the given a–t graph to construct the aligned v–t graph and x–t sketch, with coordinates at t=0,2,5,8 s and all turning points. Give signed displacement, total distance and the intervals of increasing/decreasing speed. A display claims the zero-acceleration segment means the trolley is stopped. Explain the error and check the final position by signed areas.

Four independent straight-track logs use one east-positive axis. A is explicitly uniform acceleration: v changes from +36 km/h to −18 km/h in 3000 ms. B starts from rest and has constant acceleration, travelling 27 m east in 3 s. C has constant acceleration, velocity +2 m/s at x=0 and +8 m/s at x=15 m. D reports only v(0)=+3 m/s and v(2 s)=−11 m/s, with continuous but otherwise unknown velocity. Choose the appropriate physical relation for each, compute the signed accelerations that can be established, and rank their average magnitudes. Which has the greatest guaranteed constant-acceleration magnitude among A–C? Can D be ranked by peak instantaneous acceleration from its data alone? A supervisor applies Δv/Δt directly to all four without any further equations. Explain the missing information and why the chosen relations are valid.

Three carts move along an east-positive rail. Graph A is a straight line from (0 min,0 km/h) to (2 min,36 km/h). Graph B is horizontal at +6 m/s from 0 to 100 s. Graph C is a straight line from (0 min,+18 km/h) to (1 min,+54 km/h). Treat each graph as its full observation interval, with no other motion counted. Decide independently whether each claim is true, giving a numerical or physical warrant: (i) all three cover equal distances; (ii) all have equal average speeds; (iii) C's constant acceleration is twice A's; (iv) equal distances imply equal acceleration histories. In (iv), distinguish a counterexample from a restatement. Then a technician shifts every ordinate of C downward by 36 km/h but keeps its time axis unchanged. Explain which of (i) and (iii) remains true, and why.
